summary: Solid, production-plausible tracing backend design with a durable ingest buffer (Kafka), centralized tail sampling workers, and ClickHouse for fast search plus object storage for cheap retention. It makes good cost/safety choices for multi-tenancy and provides clear degraded-mode levers, but some operational details (state sizing, ClickHouse/Kafka topology, and DR semantics) need tighter specification for true at-scale readiness.
strengths: Durable, low-latency ingest path with clear at-least-once semantics and trace co-location via Kafka partitioning
Strong multi-tenant controls (budgets, cardinality governance, query admission) and pragmatic storage split (ClickHouse hot + object storage cold)
weaknesses: Tail-sampling state management is underspecified for worst-case trace concurrency/out-of-order spans (memory bounds, spillover, backpressure behavior, and correctness under lag/replay)
Query/search scalability details are light (indexing strategy, high-cardinality tag behavior, ClickHouse replication/separation of ingest vs query, and cold-trace retrieval latency/SLO impact)
